deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Gründe auf denen die Reihen §176.177 beruhen' ('Grounds on which the series of §176–177 rest'). The page supplies the lemma behind series that Gauss had stated elsewhere (§176–177 of some notebook or draft; the numbering is not identifiable from this page). The 1809 bundle label is not a date: the word 'Potential' points to c. 1840 or later.

(1) Parametrisation. Take the ellipse with semi-axes 1+λ and 1−λ. Its foci are at ±2√λ, since c² = (1+λ)² − (1−λ)² = 4λ. A point with eccentric anomaly e is written as a complex number:
z = (1+λ)cos e + i(1−λ)sin e = u + λ/u, with u = e^{ie} (Joukowski map).
A second point is Z = U + λ/U with U = e^{iE}.

(2) Factorisation (step made explicit by me). Z − z = (U−u) + λ(1/U − 1/u) = (U−u)(1 − λ/(uU)).
Hence log|Z−z| = Re[log(U−u) + log(1 − λ u^{-1}/U)].

(3) Expansion (implicit step mine). Write log(U−u) = log U + log(1−u/U); Re log U = 0 because |U| = 1. Then
log|Z−z| = Re[ −Σ_{n≥1} (u/U)^n/n − Σ_{n≥1} λ^n/(n (uU)^n) ].
Since (u/U)^n = e^{−in(E−e)} and (uU)^{−n} = e^{−in(E+e)}, this gives
log|Z−z| = −Σ cos n(E−e)/n − Σ λ^n cos n(E+e)/n.
The first sum is the classical Fourier series of log|2 sin((E−e)/2)|.

(4) Pencil NB in the margin: the trick still works when the two points lie on different confocal ellipses. These are the curves |u| = const with the foci ±2√λ fixed. One then needs |u| < |U| for the first series to converge.

(5) Potential of a mass on the ellipse. Put mass de·f(e) on the element de, with
f(e) = A + Σ_{n≥1}(A_n cos ne + B_n sin ne), total mass 2πA.
The logarithmic potential is V(E) = ∫_0^{2π} f(e) log|Z−z| de. Use the orthogonality integrals (mine):
- ∫ cos ne cos n(E∓e) de = π cos nE;
- ∫ sin ne cos n(E−e) de = π sin nE;
- ∫ sin ne cos n(E+e) de = −π sin nE.
This yields
V(E) = −π Σ (1/n)[(1+λ^n)A_n cos nE + (1−λ^n)B_n sin nE].
The constant A contributes nothing. This matches the page.

(6) The same mass concentrated at the centre. Its potential is
2πA·log|Z| = 2πA·Re log(U + λ/U) = 2πA·Re log(1 + λU^{−2}) = 2πA Σ (−1)^{n+1} λ^n cos 2nE / n
= 2πA(λ cos2E − ½λ² cos4E + ⅓λ³ cos6E − …).

Purpose, as continued on the next page: equate (5) and (6) on the ellipse. This gives A_{2n} = 4A(−1)^n λ^n/(1+λ^{2n}), all other coefficients zero. The result is the 'swept' (balayage) distribution of the central point mass onto the ellipse, i.e. the density of harmonic measure of the ellipse interior seen from its centre. Its integral p(e) leads on the next page to a function t (theta-function quotient, with μ² = λ) whose imaginary part of log is p. In effect t is the conformal map of the elliptic disc onto the unit disc.
errors: In the second series the first term appears as λu/(uU). It should be λ/(uU), consistent with the following terms λλ/(uuUU) and λ³/(u³U³). This is either a pen slip or a misreading.

The series in u/U is used with |u| = |U| = 1, i.e. on the circle of convergence. It converges only conditionally (diverging at E = e) and is valid as a Fourier series. This is standard but not justified on the page.
The trailing sign of the last series is ambiguous ('+∓'). The correct continuation is −¼λ⁴cos8E …, alternating.

results.what: Fourier expansion of the logarithmic kernel between two points of an ellipse (or of confocal ellipses), via the Joukowski parametrisation z = u + λ/u: log|Z−z| = −Σ[cos n(E−e) + λ^n cos n(E+e)]/n
results.modern_name: Fourier/multipole expansion of the 2D logarithmic kernel in elliptic coordinates; Joukowski map
results.usually_credited_to: Classical potential theory, 19th century (elliptic-coordinate expansions; Joukowski 1910 for the map in aerodynamics)

results.what: Logarithmic potential on the ellipse of a Fourier-series mass density on the ellipse: −π Σ (1/n)[(1+λ^n)A_n cos nE + (1−λ^n)B_n sin nE]
results.modern_name: Single-layer logarithmic potential on an ellipse / spectral decomposition of the logarithmic potential operator on an ellipse

results.what: Preparation for equating with the potential of a central point mass, yielding the balayage (harmonic measure from the centre) of the ellipse and, on the next page, the theta-quotient conformal map of the elliptic disc onto the circle
results.modern_name: Harmonic measure / Green's function of an ellipse; conformal map of ellipse interior onto disc via elliptic functions
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (1869) for the ellipse–disc conformal map by elliptic functions

deep.surprise_reason: The computation on this page is routine Fourier analysis of the log kernel. Its purpose is less routine: harmonic measure of an ellipse, and on the next page the theta-function conformal map of an ellipse onto a disc. That map is usually credited to Schwarz (1869). Gauss's conformal-mapping and theta-function work makes this plausible but not widely known as his.

checkable.asserts: The ellipse point equals u + λ/u with u = e^{ie} (should simplify to 0).
Cosine part of the potential: π(1+λ^n)cos nE (each entry 0).
Sine part of the potential: π(1−λ^n)sin nE (each entry 0).
Expected to equal λcos2E − λ²cos4E/2 + λ³cos6E/3 + O(λ⁴). The 're' may need expanding (e.g. as log|1+λe^{−2iE}|) for sympy to produce this.
Coefficient of the equilibrating density: A_{2n} = 4A(−1)^n λ^n/(1+λ^{2n}), as on the next page.

transcription_corrections: Second series, first term: likely λ/(uU), not λu/(uU).
'in jedem{+dem+} Punkte': read as the insertion 'in dem Punkte' (in the point) with 'jedem' deleted or altered.
Header pencil mark after '222' is an illegible pencil annotation, not part of the text.
End of last line: the stray '+' / '∓' should be read as the continuing alternating series ('−…').
